results.title: Special session of 7th World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue concludesJoint Session of International Organizations and Ministers focuses on addressing disinformation and protecting cultural heritage
results.description: Baku, October 27, AZERTACThe second part of the Special Joint Session of the 3rd High-Level Meeting of International Organizations and 6th Ministerial Meeting of the Baku Process was held on October 27 as part of the 7th World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue, themed “Dialogue for a Shared Future”. The session, titled “From Partnership to Collective Action: Strengthening Global Synergy for Intercultural Dialogue in the AI Era” brought together high-ranking officials, parliamentary leaders, religious figures, scholars, journalists, and representatives of various ethnic and cultural groups. At a session moderated by Elman Abdullayev, Secretary-General of the National Commission of the Republic of Azerbaijan for UNESCO, Sudan’s Minister of Culture, Information and Tourism Khalid Ismail Ahmed Ali highlighted technology’s role in promoting cultural heritage, stressing the need for its responsible use to combat misinformation and bias. Other participants, including ministers, diplomats and representatives of international organizations, discussed how AI and modern technologies can advance intercultural dialogue, preserve cultural heritage, strengthen mutual understanding and promote peace. They also emphasized international cooperation, joint initiatives, reliable information and the fight against disinformation. The event emphasized youth engagement, expanded educational and creative opportunities, respect for cultural diversity, and the role of digital technologies in promoting intercultural dialogue. Speakers highlighted the need for practical international cooperation to address global challenges, preserve cultural heritage and promote sustainable peace. Held on October 27–29, the Forum is organized by Azerbaijan’s Ministry of Culture in partnership with UNAOC, UNESCO, UN Tourism and ICESCO as part of the Baku Process, launched in 2008 at President Ilham Aliyev’s initiative.
